links.comparator_used: German standard double reading by two radiologists (programme performance)
links.outcome: Cancer detection rate, recall rate and reading workload
links.effect: Standalone AI replacing both readers: CDR 6.37 (95% CI 6.10-6.64) vs programme 6.32 per 1000, non-inferior, recall 3.80 vs 4.11 per 100. Single reader replacement: CDR 6.49 (6.31-6.67), recall 4.01 (3.92-4.10), 49% workload reduction.
links.quote: Compared with the German screening programme (CDR 6·32 per 1000 examinations, recall rate 4·11 per 100 examinations), replacement of both readers (standalone AI strategy) achieved a non-inferior CDR of 6·37 (95% CI 6·10-6·64) at a recall rate of 3·80 (95% CI 3·67-3·93), whereas single reader replacement achieved a CDR of 6·49 (6·31-6·67), a recall rate of 4·01 (3·92-4·10), and a 49% workload reduction.

links.comparator_used: Standard double reading of all examinations (German screening programme), plus other AI integration strategies
links.outcome: Cancer detection rate, recall rate and reading workload
links.effect: Programme-level decision referral: CDR 6.85 (6.61-7.11) vs 6.32 programme, recall 3.55 (3.43-3.68) vs 4.11, 84% workload reduction. In Sweden, CDR increased by 17.7% without increasing recall and reading workload fell by 92%.
links.quote: Programme-level decision referral achieved a CDR of 6·85 (6·61-7·11), a recall rate of 3·55 (3·43-3·68), and an 84% workload reduction.

design_hint: AI integration strategies (decision referral, reader replacement, triaging)
